subject: Log custody, egress windows and deletion attestation — Q&A
messages:
From: Mike Turner <mike.turner@greenfieldhealth.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Greenfield Health Security <security@greenfieldhealth.com>, legal@greenfieldhealth.com
Date: Thu, 8 Jul 2028 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Logs handoff windows, deletion attestation, and export format questions

Hi Hannah,

Quick set of questions from our compliance team as we close the procurement: can Redwood provide a short write-up that covers (1) how long audit/access logs are retained by default and under reserved capacity, (2) options and lead times for exporting raw logs (bulk egress), and (3) the format and cryptographic proof we would receive that logs were deleted at our request? We need this for our legal and security sign-off.

We'd ideally like an example export (schema + a tiny sample) and an attestation template indicating deletion occurred. Any restrictions on timelines or cross-border egress we should expect?

Thanks — happy to jump on a short call if easier.

— Mike Turner
Dir, IT Risk & Compliance
Greenfield Health
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Mike Turner <mike.turner@greenfieldhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 9 Jul 2028 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Logs handoff windows, deletion attestation, and export format questions

Hi Mike — thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front, longer detail below and attached: audit_manifest_2028-07-08.csv and export_sample_2028-07-09.jsonl.

1) Retention: Hosted defaults to 90 days for access/audit logs; Dedicated customers can request 365-day retention as part of the Dedicated contract (we mirror that to the retention SLA). Private on-prem/VPC deployments are customer-configurable.

2) Bulk export windows: We support scheduled and ad-hoc bulk exports. Typical lead time for >100GB exports is 48–72 hours for hosted customers (we provision a temporary egress job). For Dedicated customers we can do same-day exports for typical sizes under agreed burst capacity. Exports are delivered encrypted to a customer S3 bucket (or secure FTP) via temporary presigned URL.

3) Deletion attestation: After a verified deletion request we provide a signed attestation PDF and an operation log showing the job id, objects removed, and time window. For hosted tenants we also provide a tombstone manifest showing indices removed from long-term cold storage. For Private deployments the deletion statement is customer-self-administered unless a Managed Support engagement is in place.

Cross-border notes: by default exports follow the customer region; cross-border egress requires a signed data transfer addendum for EU ↔ US movement.

I'll loop in Karthik for the export schema details and Marissa for the attestation wording. If you want a short call Mon/Tue let me know availability.

Best,
Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Adding the attestation side — for enterprise/Dedicated we include deletion attestation as part of our SLA playbook. Typical contents of the attestation:
- Reference to job id and tenant id
- List of object keys removed (or index ranges)
- Time window of deletion and storage tier affected
- Signatory from Redwood's Ops (name + title)
- Hash of the delivered manifest (SHA256) and signature metadata

We have a template attestation (PDF) we can share; it includes our standard legal language and escalation contact. If Greenfield needs an expanded statement (e.g., third-party notarization), we can scope that as an add-on.

— Marissa
VP, Customer Success
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Mike Turner <mike.turner@greenfieldhealth.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 11 Jul 2028 08:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Logs handoff windows, deletion attestation, and export format questions

Hi all — technical details on the export payload and deletion proof. See attached s3-egress-policy.pdf for transfer mechanics. Summary:

- Export formats: JSONL (each event per line), compressed with gzip. For very large exports (>500GB) we shard into numbered parts (export_YYYYMMDD_0001.jsonl.gz). Each event includes timestamp, tenant_id, request_id, actor (internal/external), action, resource, outcome, and metadata fields.
- Delivery: we push encrypted artifacts to your S3 bucket using server-side encryption on Redwood side; once transfer completes we rotate a short-lived presigned URL for download. We support customer-side KMS keys (BYOK) for end-to-end encryption.
- Integrity: Every artifact is accompanied by a manifest.jsonl.sha256 file and a manifest.sig (signature with our private key). You can verify the SHA256 checksums and validate the signature against our published verification key.
- Deletion attestation process: Step 1: Customer opens a deletion request (ticket) and provides scope (time range/tenant or object keys). Step 2: We schedule deletion job and produce a pre-deletion snapshot (kept encrypted for 72 hours as a rollback window). Step 3: After job completes we publish a deletion report (manifest of removed keys + SHA256) and a signed attestation PDF. Step 4: On request we can run a verification job that samples the removed object keys and produces a proof-of-erasure log (hash chain).

Command-line example (for demonstration only):
- aws s3 cp s3://redwood-exports/greenfield/export_20280709_0001.jsonl.gz ./ --region us-west-2 --sse aws:kms

Notes on timing: hosted export job provisioning is typically 48–72 hrs; Dedicated customers with burst capacity can be same-day. Deletion attestation PDFs are generated within 24 hours of job completion; notarization is a separate service.

Happy to attach a tiny sample export (we included export_sample_2028-07-09.jsonl in the Drive link).

— Karthik
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
